newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks end strong on economic reports.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks end strong on economic reports.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks soared Tuesday, powered by a strong performance in the bond market on new evidence that the economy is still growing at a moderate pace.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended 49.54 points higher at 7,722.33.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,691 to 1,133 on active volume of 544 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The good news came from the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) monthly survey, which showed an increase in manufacturing activity in June, though at a slower pace than economists had expected.
The data soothed recent jitters over the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy meeting, which began Tuesday and concludes on Wednesday.
"I don't think anybody's scared at this point," said Arnie Owen, managing director of capital markets at Cruttenden Roth. "I certainly don't think anyone sees any inflation out there."

The bond market also shot higher on the NAPM report, sending the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury up 18/32, or $5.625 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.74 percent from 6.79 percent Monday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Stocks quickly followed, led by interest rate-sensitive sectors like finance and transportation.
Among financial stocks, J.P. Morgan & Co. rose 3-1/8 to 107-1/2 and Travelers Group Inc. gained 1-5/8 to 64-11/16.
Airlines were among the strongest performers, with Delta Air Lines Inc. rising 1-13/16 to 84-7/16 and Southwest Airlines Co. leaping 1-5/8 to 27-1/2.

Early in the day, Southwest was cited on Lehman Brothers' annual list of 10 "uncommon values," a portfolio of stocks the firm believes will outperform the Standard & Poor's 500 index over the next 12 months.
While Wall Street is nearly unanimous in expecting the Fed will leave interest rates steady, it still faces a critical test in the monthly data on payrolls and wages.
The report is due out Thursday instead of its traditional Friday release because of the Independence Day-shortened work week.
Between the employment figures and the Fed meeting, analysts said market action could be quite contained.
"In the past we've hesitated before employment reports and before Fed meetings, and this week we have both," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at Everen Securities.

Among individual issues, Office Depot Inc. tumbled 3-13/16 to 15-5/8 in the first trading since Monday's court ruling striking down the company's plans to merge with Staples Inc., whose stock rose 1-1/16 to 24-5/16.
Boeing Co. gained 1 at 54-1/16 after the company won unconditional approval from U.S. regulators for its merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp. McDonnell Douglas rose 1-3/16 to 69-11/16.

Pierce Leahy Corp. jumped 5-9/16 to 23-9/16 in its New York Stock Exchange debut. Pierce Leahy, based in King of Prussia, Pa., manages archived records including paper records, microfilm and videotapes.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 3.82 points to 1,438.25.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 5.89 to 891.03. The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.04 to 625.61.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.57 to 466.01. The average share was up 34 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,441,426 up 44.556, or 0.53 percent.
